ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.claim: Al-Ḥāqqah resembles the preceding al-Wāqiʿah in affirming the Resurrection and depicting its terrors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r1.anchor: both substantiate the Day of Judgement and portray the horrors of that Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r2.claim: Both sūrahs describe the outcomes for the companions of the right and left hands.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r2.anchor: both mention the details of the fate met by the companions of the right hand

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r6.claim: A person destined for Hell among the monotheists may receive the record in the right hand on display day and find it a comfort during punishment; another view delays it until leaving Hell, with faith as comfort meanwhile.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r6.anchor: أنه في يوم العرض يأخذ كتابه بيمينه مع الناجين من النار، ويكون ذلك يأنس به مدة العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r7.claim: The delayed-record view is argued to fit better, since someone being led to Hell would not joyfully invite others to read his book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r7.anchor: فلا يناسب دخول النار. وهاؤم إن كان مدلولها خذ، فهي متسلطة على كتابيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.claim: Most readers retain hāʾ al-sakt in the connected and paused forms for book, reckoning, wealth, and power, and also in mā hiyah in al-Qāriʿah.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: كتابيه، وحسابيه في موضعيهما وماليه وسلطانيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin deletes the hāʾ and silences the yāʾ; Ibn Abī Isḥāq and al-Aʿmash delete it only in connected speech, while Ḥamza does so for selected forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن: بحذفها وصلا ووقفا وإسكان الياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.claim: Al-Zuhrawī calls retaining hāʾ in connected speech an error, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because the transmitted reading is mass-transmitted and must be accepted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r11.anchor: ليس كما قال، بل ذلك منقول نقل التواتر فوجب قبوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r11.claim: After seeing his evil deeds and fate, he wishes he had not received his record or learned his account, which has exposed what harms rather than benefits him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p261/r11.anchor: لما رأى فيه قبائح أفعاله وما يصير أمره إليه، تمنى أنه لم يعطه، وتمنى أنه لم يدر حسابه

RAZI-FULL:v30p100/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p100/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p100/r1.claim: Seeing the record of his shameful deeds makes the spiritual torment of humiliation worse than fire; the sinner wishes he had been burned instead of shown his record.
RAZI-FULL:v30p100/r1.anchor: لما نظر في كتابه وتذكر قبائح أفعاله خجل منها وصار العذاب الحاصل من تلك الخجالة أزيد من عذاب النار

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r16.claim: Those given the book in the left hand are cast into Hell for their deeds.
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r16.anchor: Those given the book in the left hand will be cast into Hell for their deeds

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r17.claim: The account of receiving the record from behind the back in 84:10–12 is reconciled by saying the left hand is tied behind the back.
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r17.anchor: To reconcile v. 25 and 84:10, commentators say that the left hand will be tied behind the back

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r18.claim: The wish not to receive the book may express a desire to avoid punishment altogether.
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r18.anchor: Would that I had not been given may imply a desire to avoid punishment altogether

STUDYQURAN:69:19/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r19.claim: Alternatively, the shame of seeing one’s deeds may be worse than the Fire’s pain, making it preferable to enter Hell without judgment.
STUDYQURAN:69:19/r19.anchor: it may indicate that the shame at witnessing one’s deeds is worse than the pain of the Fire

TABATABAI:69:19-26/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:19-26/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:19-26/r8.claim: The left-hand recipients are the wretched criminals; seeing their painful punishment, they wish they had neither received the record nor learned their account, as previously discussed in al-Isrāʾ.
TABATABAI:69:19-26/r8.anchor: وهؤلاء هم الطائفة الثانية وهم الأشقياء المجرمون يؤتون صحيفة أعمالهم بشمالهم

TABATABAI:69:13-37/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:13-37/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:13-37/r6.claim: Reports that apply the right-hand record to Ali or Ali and his Shi'a, and the left-hand record to his enemies, are instances of application (jary), not exegesis.
TABATABAI:69:13-37/r6.anchor: وفي عدة من الروايات تطبيق قوله { فأما من أوتي كتابه بيمينه } الخ، على علي عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r1.claim: Receiving the record in the left hand humiliates the sinner: his left hand is twisted behind his back to take it, exposing his ugly deeds.
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r1.anchor: {وأما من أوتى كتابه بشماله} تحقيرا له لأن الشمال يتشاءم بها

BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r2.claim: His words express grief, regret, and fear; this spiritual pain is more severe than bodily pain.
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r2.anchor: تحزنا وتحسرا وخوفا مما فيه وهو من قبيل الألم الروحاني الذي هو أشد من الألم الجسمني

BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r3.claim: The passive form means that he was not given the record.
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r3.anchor: مجهول منا لإيتاء بمعنى لم أعط

BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p109#2/r4.claim: He calls it his book because it has gathered all his evil deeds.

THALABI:v10p30/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p30/r7.speaker: ابن الثابت
THALABI:v10p30/r7.claim: Ibn al-Thabit says the left hand is twisted behind the person's back before the book is given to him.
THALABI:v10p30/r7.anchor: قال ابن الثابت: تلوى يده اليسرى خلف ظهره ثم يعطى كتابه.

THALABI:v10p30/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p30/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p30/r8.claim: Another view says the hand is pulled from his chest behind his back to receive the book.
THALABI:v10p30/r8.anchor: وقيل: تنزع من صدره إلى خلف ظهره فيقول يا ليتني لم أوت كتابيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p174/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p174/r1.speaker: عطاء ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p174/r1.claim: ʿAta and Muqatil say the verse was revealed about al-Aswad ibn al-Asad al-Makhzumi, brother of the man associated with the right-hand record; Hamza killed him at Badr.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p174/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p174/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p174/r2.claim: The angel who recorded his deeds in worldly life gives him the book, and he wishes he had not received it when he sees his shameful deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p174/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعطيه ملكه الذي كتب عمله في الدنيا

QASHANI:69:25/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:25/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:25/r1.claim: Receiving the book in the left hand signifies the weaker, animal-soul side.

QASHANI:69:25/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:25/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:25/r2.claim: Seeing the recorded ugly forms and deeds makes him recoil, regret his life, wish for death, and realize that wealth, power, and status harmed rather than helped him.
QASHANI:69:25/r2.anchor: فيتحسر ويتندم ويتوحش من تلك الصور والهيئات السمجة والقبائح التي نسيها وأحصاها الله

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r6.claim: Yamīn, opposite shimāl, means the right hand or side and connotes strength, honesty, propriety, purity, good fortune, good, and gain.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r6.anchor: Burada “yemîn”, “şimal” mukabili olduğundan sağ el, sağ taraf demektir ki sağlamlık, dürüstlük, uygunluk, temizlik, uğur, hayr ve kesb ifade eder.

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r7.claim: Right-hand action symbolizes acting properly for oneself; the left signals the reverse, while putting something behind means neglect or leaving it to others. The imagery also places good-deed angels to the right, bad-deed angels to the left, and associates the angel/right and Satan/left.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r7.anchor: Sağ eliyle yapması sağlam, dürüst, uygun, kendi lehinde iyi yapması; sol eliyle yapması da tersine yapması; arkaya atması ise ihmal etmesi, başkasından umması mânalarını ifade eder.

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r8.claim: Saying the book is given, rather than self-written, reflects that God's enabling, decree, judgment, and execution govern the outcome.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r8.anchor: “Verilmesi” tâbiri dahi hepsi Allah’ın tevfîki, takdîri

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r9.claim: Although creation and command belong to God, responsibility is tied to voluntary deeds: by choosing them, a person effectively dictates the record to the angels like a scribe.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r9.anchor: insanın mes’ûliyeti ihtiyârî fiillerine rabtedilmiş olduğu cihetle

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r12.claim: Someone who never audits himself has put the matter behind him, dictating a record heedlessly and without considering the harm.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r12.anchor: Vicdânında her gün Hakk’a karşı nefsini muhasebe etmeyen kimse işini arkaya atmış

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r13.claim: Those who distort right and wrong fill the record with bad deeds and liabilities; angels record facts faithfully, so the wrongdoer has signed his own destiny against himself.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r13.anchor: meleklerin tuttuğu zabıt onun aleyhinde olarak muameleyi olduğu gibi göstermiş ve ona imza ettirilmiş olmak haysiyetiyle sağlam, doğru ve haddizâtında muteber bulunduğundan

ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r1.claim: The believer's account is reviewed by a friend and its verdict handed over favorably; the disbeliever's is reviewed by a hated opponent and given against him in the left hand.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r1.anchor: huzûr-i Hak’ta yüzü ak olarak hesâbı dost tarafından görülmüş

ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r16.claim: Some do ostensibly good works for people, ostentation, or others' pleasure rather than God; rewards from people disappear like a bankrupt's assets, leaving only pain and deprivation before God.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r16.anchor: hayır denebilecek şeyler yaparlar amma Hak için Allah için değil

ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r17.claim: Their deeds end in loss, so these are people who wrote their books backward and left-handed.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#2/r17.anchor: Bütün o Hâkka onların başında patlar

ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.claim: The final hā in kitābiyeh, hisābiyeh, māliyeh, and sultāniyeh is hāʾ al-sakt, used at pause after fatḥa and always read with sukūn; the underlying forms end in -iya.
ELMALILI:69:18-29#3/r4.anchor: “Kitâbiyeh, hisâbiyeh, mâliyeh, sultâniyeh” fâsılalarında ها fetha üzerine vakf için hâ-i sekittir. Dâima sâkin okunur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r1.claim: Receiving the record on the left signifies disobedience to God, a dishonest and unvirtuous life, and a corrupt record.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r1.anchor: amel defterinin sol tarafından verilmesi onun dünya hayatında Allah’ın emrine uygun hareket etmediğini, dürüst ve erdemli bir hayat yaşamadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r2.claim: Seeing his deeds in the record, the person understands punishment is coming, does not want to see what is written, and wishes death had ended everything.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:25/r2.anchor: bu sebeple amel defterinin kendisine verilmesini ve içinde yazılmış olanları görmek istemez, ölümle her şeyin bitmiş olmasını temenni eder

BURHAN:v1p364/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p364/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p364/r5.claim: Some wording is constructed to require a pause, as in the speaker's wish that he had not received his record; the author contrasts a complete-stop example ending in nār ḥāmiyah.
BURHAN:v1p364/r5.anchor: ومنها أن يكون الكلام مبنيا على الوقف فلا يجوز فيه إلا الوقف صيغة كقوله ﴿ يا ليتني لم أوت كتابيه

BURHAN:v4p430/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p430/r7.speaker: حمزة
BURHAN:v4p430/r7.claim: The readers retain hāʾ in connection in كتابيه and حسابيه on pausal intent; Hamza deletes it in three other words when connecting but retains it at a stop.

ITQAN:v1p229#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r6.claim: Some speech is composed to be heard with a pause, as the speaker’s lament over receiving his record continues into the next verse.
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r6.anchor: نحو ﴿ يا ليتني لم أوت كتابيه ولم أدر ما حسابيه ﴾

TUSTARI:69:25/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:69:25/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:69:25/r1.claim: The left-handed person's record contains evil deeds and disbelief, so he wishes he had never been resurrected.
TUSTARI:69:25/r1.anchor: أي بما فيه من الأعمال الخبيثة والكفر، فيتمنى أن يكون غير مبعوث

NAHHAS:v5p21/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p21/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p21/r15.claim: Some Arabs drop the nūn in ليتني, as they do after إن.
NAHHAS:v5p21/r15.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول ليتني فيحذف النون كما يحذفها في إن

NAHHAS:v5p21/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p21/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p21/r16.claim: Hāʾ is retained at pause to clarify the vowel; retaining it in connected speech is faulty by grammarians known to the author. Following the written rasm and pausing avoids error.
NAHHAS:v5p21/r16.anchor: بإثبات الهاء في الوقف وكذا ما لبيان الحركة وإثباتها في الوصل لحن لا يجوز

ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n14/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n14/r1.claim: Receiving the record in the left hand signifies an unrighteous earthly life, in contrast with receiving it in the right hand.
ASAD-NOTES:69:25#n14/r1.anchor: signifying that he had been unrighteous in his earthly life, in contrast with those "whose record will be placed in their right hand"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r1.claim: Exegetes differ over the mockers’ request to have their record hastened: some connect it to the records given in right or left hands, others to seeing their afterlife homes, and others to hastening punishment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r1.anchor: وإنما اختلف أهل التأويل في معنى مسألة المشركين ربهم التعجيل لهم بكتابهم على وجه الاستهزاء والاستخفاف

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r2.claim: The author links the relevant expression to the root sense of cutting; the third consonant differentiates related forms by what is cut.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r2.anchor: وإن ردوها إلى القطع وهو الأصل. ومنه استعمال حرف قط في النفي البات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r3.claim: The word maqṭūṭ in al-Aʿshā’s poetic example is agreed to mean award documents or letters of grants.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p362/r3.anchor: وأما "المقطوط" في الشاهد من بيت الأعشى، فلم يختلفوا في أن معناها صكوك الجوائز

NASHR:v2p142/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p142/r6.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p142/r6.claim: Yaʿqūb omits the hāʾ of kitābiyah and ḥisābiyah in connection but retains it in pause; the other readers retain it in both positions.
NASHR:v2p142/r6.anchor: كلاهما فحذف الهاء منهما وصلا وأثبتها وقفا يعقوب

QIRAAT-ER:69:25:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:25:14#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:69:25:14#1/r1.claim: The canonical ten variants permit forms with or without full hāʾ al-sakt, allowing variation in the trailing vowel.
QIRAAT-ER:69:25:14#1/r1.anchor: Canonical ten variant allowing both forms — with and without full hāʾ al-sakt

ALUSI-FULL:v29p48#5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p48#5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p48#5/r1.claim: Seeing the ugliness of his deeds and the reckoning reveal what grieves him, the left-handed person wishes he had never received his book or known his account.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p48#5/r1.anchor: لما يرى من قبح العمل وانجلاء الحساب عما يسوءه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r2.speaker: ابن السائب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r2.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says the left hand is twisted from the chest behind the person's back before the book is given.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r2.anchor: قال ابن السائب: تلوى يده اليسرى [من صدره] (1) خلف ظهره ثم يعطى كتابه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r3.claim: Another report says the left hand is pulled from the chest behind the back, and then the book is handed over.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r3.anchor: وقيل: تنزع يده اليسرى من صدره إلى خلف ظهره ثم يعطى كتابه؛

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r4.claim: Seeing the shameful deeds in his record makes him wish he had never received it or learned his reckoning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p212/r4.anchor: يتمنى أنه لم يؤت كتابه لما يرى فيه من قبائح أعماله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r1.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r1.claim: Burayda reports the Prophet saying al-Baqara's recitation is blessing, abandoning it regret, and magicians cannot withstand it; al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān shade their companion, while Qur'an rewards the devoted reader and parents and raises the reader through Paradise. Baghawī grades this report gharīb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r1.anchor: عن أبيه قال كنت جالسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسمعته يقول: " اقرءوا سورة البقرة فإن أخذها بركة وتركها حسرة ولا يستطيعها البطلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r2.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r2.claim: The Prophet says that whoever listens to a Qur'anic verse receives a multiplied good deed, and whoever recites a verse will have a light on Judgment Day; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r2.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من استمع إلى آية من كتاب الله عز وجل كتبت له حسنة مضاعفة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r3.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r3.claim: The Prophet says three verses recited in prayer are better than three large pregnant camels returned to their owner; Baghawī grades the report ṣaḥīḥ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p42/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أيحب أحدكم إذا رجع إلى أهله أن يجد فيه ثلاث خلفات

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r1.claim: Seeing the ugliness of his deeds and the bad outcome leads the recipient of the book in his left hand to regret it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r1.anchor: لما يرى من قبح العمل وسوء العاقبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:25-29/r2.claim: He wishes he had never received his record.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r1.claim: After first presenting the accepted person to encourage hope, the passage presents the rejected person to warn against his deeds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r1.anchor: وذكر سبحانه وتعالى المقبول بادئا به تشويقا إلى حاله وتغبيطا بعاقبته وحسن مآله , أتبعه المردود تنفيرا عن أعماله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r2.claim: The passive “was given” stresses the humiliation of receiving an unwanted outcome and his inability to refuse it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r2.anchor: بانيا للمفعول لذلك وللدلالة على ذل الأخذ وعدم قدرته على الامتناع عن شيء يسوءه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r3.claim: He speaks after the veil is lifted and he sees the certainty of his fate and the evil deeds he had committed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r3.anchor: لما يرى من سوء عاقبته التي كشف له عنها الغطاء حتى لم يشك فيها لما يرى من قبائحه التي قدمها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r4.claim: Any apparent hesitation in the condemned person’s speech is stubborn, false argument and resistance of the kind he practiced in worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r4.anchor: وكل ما يأتي مما يوهم سكتة في ذلك اليوم فمن باب المكابرة والمدافعة بالباطل على ما كان عليه في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r5.claim: He wishes impossibly that he had received no record and had never learned what his reckoning—his deeds and their recompense—would be.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r5.anchor: تمنيا للمحال , وجرى عن نسق ما مضى في البناء للمفعول الدال على ذله وعدم جبلته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r6.claim: The reckoning includes an account of the deeds and their recompense; he wishes he had remained ignorant as he was in this world.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p133/r6.anchor: من ذكر العمل وذكر جزائه , بل استمريت جاهلا لذلك كما كنت في الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r8.claim: Verses 25–29 counterpose the person given his book in his right hand at 69:19; the left-hand recipient’s fate is understood from that contrast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r8.anchor: هذا قسيم { من أوتي كتابه بيمينه } ( الحاقة : 19 ) ، فالقول في إيتائه كتابه بشماله قد عرف وجهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r9.claim: The left-hand recipient wishes he had not received his book because it revealed his punishment; he wishes to avoid the grief of learning what awaits him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p134/r9.anchor: وتمني كل من أوتي كتابه بشماله أنه لم يؤت كتابه ، لأنه علم من الاطلاع على كتابه أنه صائر إلى العذاب فيتمنى أن لا يكون علم بذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r7.speaker: بعض
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r7.claim: One view says sinful believers take their books with everyone else, which comforts them during their punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم الأظهر أنها تأخذها مع الناس، وذلك يؤنسها مدة العذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says they do not read their books until God permits them, then they call others to read them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r8.anchor: قال الحسن: فإذا أعطى كتابه بيمينه لم يقرأه حتى يأذن الله تعالى له، فإذا أذن له قال: هاؤم اقرؤا كتابيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r9.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r9.claim: Another view says sinful believers receive their books after being brought out of Hell, with faith consoling them during punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: الأظهر أنه إذا أخرجوا من النار والإيمان يؤنسهم وقت العذاب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r1.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Aswad, whom Ḥamza killed at Badr; he was Abū Salama's brother.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل نزلت في الأسود بن عبد الأسود قتله حمزة ببدر وهو أخو أبي سلمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r2.claim: Another account says the verse was revealed about Abū Jahl.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r3.claim: He wishes he had not received his book because of the repulsive deeds he sees recorded in it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p352#6/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى يا ليتني لم أوت كتابيه وذلك لما يرى فيه من القباحج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r1.claim: The wretched person receives his record in his left hand at the gathering place and then regrets it intensely, wishing he had never received it or learned his reckoning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p215#2/r1.anchor: إذا أعطي أحدهم كتابه في العرصات بشماله، فحينئذ يندم غاية الندم، فيقول:

JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.claim: Hamza and Yaqub drop the final h in connection for māliyah, sulṭāniyah, and mā hiyah in al-Qāriʿa; all retain it at pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة ويعقوب: ماليه وسلطانيه وفي سورة (القارعة) (ما هيه) بحذف الهاء في الوصل،

JISHUMI:v10p7060/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r7.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r7.claim: Yaqub alone drops final h in connection for these forms; others retain it in connection, and everyone retains it at pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7060/r7.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وحده: اقرأوا كتابيه، ملاق حسابيه، لم أوت كتابيه، ما حسابيه بحذف الهاء في الوصل،

JISHUMI:v10p7061/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7061/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7061/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the left-hand book passage revealed concerning Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Asad.
JISHUMI:v10p7061/r3.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (وأما من أوتي كتابه بشماله) في شأن أبي سلمة بن عبد الأسد، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v10p7061/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7061/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7061/r4.claim: The author prefers the passage is general, with Abu Salama included.
JISHUMI:v10p7061/r4.anchor: وقيل: بل هو عام، وهو الصحيح، وذلك الرجل داخل في الجملة.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r1.claim: The left-hand recipient may be voicing his wish hopefully; alternatively, he had been concealed and is now exposed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r1.anchor: أنه كان يقول ذلك راجيا . الثاني : أنه كان مستورا فافتضح

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r2.claim: Arab convention uses the right for acceptance and honor, and the left for rejection and humiliation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p84/r2.anchor: ومن عادة العرب أن تفرق بين القبول والرد وبين الكرامة والهوان

MUQATIL:69:25-32/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r1.claim: The one given his book in his left hand receives it from the angel who recorded his worldly deeds.
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r1.anchor: يقول: يعطيه ملكه الذي كان يكتب عمله في الدنيا نزلت هذه الآية في الاسود

MUQATIL:69:25-32/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Aswad al-Makhzumi, whom Hamza b. Abd al-Muttalib killed at the watering place at Badr.
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r2.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في الاسود المخزومي قتله حمزة بن عبدالمطلب على الحوض ببدر

MUQATIL:69:25-32/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r3.claim: He wishes he had not received his book, had not known his reckoning, and that death had ended his life.
MUQATIL:69:25-32/r3.anchor: فيتمنى في الآخرة { لم أوت كتابيه } [آية: 25] { ولم أدر ما حسابيه } [آية: 26] { يليتها كانت القاضية }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p276/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p276/r1.claim: He wishes he had not received his record because of the disgraceful things he sees in it.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r1.claim: The condemned man wishes he had not received his record, did not know his reckoning, and that death had ended everything; he longs for death.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:25-34/r1.anchor: وهو يقول: { يليتني لم أوت كتابيه ولم أدر ما حسابيه يليتها كانت القاضية } يتمنى الموت.
